depth_justification: Reacts to Lunara's specific disclosures (6.5/1.8 Pearl Index from N=1500, the Bayesian model with displayed uncertainty intervals, aggregated anonymized research sharing, the sensitive-data onboarding flow, EU+CH) and cites the precise applicable rules (GDPR Art. 9(2)(a) explicit consent, Art. 5(1)(c), MDR, EU AI Act); held back by verbatim repetition of P1.D7/P2.D4/P3.D2 blocks and a too-soft MDR stance for a contraception predictor.
actionability_justification: Multiple concrete recipes (AES-256 at rest / TLS 1.3 in transit, a separate sensitive-data consent toggle distinct from general consent, CSV/JSON data export, k-anonymity/differential privacy, error-reporting mechanisms) plus the requested severity-grouped report, though some items remain directional and the final report is truncated mid-sentence.
salient_examples: Implement encryption at rest and in transit (e.g., AES-256, TLS 1.3)
A Pearl Index of 6.5 in typical use indicates that 6.5 out of 100 women ... would become pregnant in a year
explicit consent under Article 9(2)(a) ... a clear and separate consent mechanism ... distinct from general data processing consent
Use pseudonymization or anonymization techniques such as k-anonymity, l-diversity, or differential privacy
